q: How do you scale a GenAI app to 6,000 users?
a: Convert to load (peak questions/s, LLM calls, tokens/min, concurrent streams); size API quota across regions with an LLM gateway and fallbacks, or self-hosted vLLM GPUs from load-test throughput; stateless async services; per-user rate limits; routing; caching; gradual rollout.

q: How many GPUs do you need for N users?
a: Users → peak questions/s → LLM calls → input/output tokens/s → divide by measured tokens/s per GPU at your latency target → × headroom (~1.5) → at least 2 for redundancy. The per-GPU number must come from a load test.

q: Why can one GPU serve many users with vLLM?
a: Continuous batching (requests join the running batch every step), PagedAttention (efficient KV-cache memory) and prefix caching; throughput rises with concurrency until memory or latency limits.

q: What do you do when you hit 429 rate-limit errors at peak?
a: Retry with exponential back-off and jitter; spread load across deployments/regions; fallback models via an LLM gateway; per-user rate limits and token budgets; request higher or provisioned quota; route simple questions to smaller models.

API: best quality, fast start, elastic, but quotas, per-token cost and data-residency questions. Self-hosted: control and privacy, cheaper at high steady volume, but you run GPUs, cold starts and ops.
